target.title: fix(exec): require approval for OpenClaw lifecycle commands
target.body:
﻿﻿Fixes #99518

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where exec commands through gateway or node hosts could let OpenClaw gateway/daemon lifecycle mutations pass through normal allowlist or auto-review paths when they should require explicit approval.

The affected workflow is OpenClaw self-management from exec surfaces: stopping, starting, restarting, running, deleting, or uninstalling the gateway/daemon through CLI, launchctl, systemctl, schtasks, process-kill, shell-wrapper, package-manager, Windows shim, `env -S`, `xargs`/`find`, `sudo`/`doas`, and dispatch-wrapper commands.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a focused lifecycle classifier to the exec approval policy and wires it into the main gateway-host, node-host, and direct `system.run` approval paths. The guard forces explicit approval for OpenClaw lifecycle mutations unless exec is already in yolo mode (`security=full`, `ask=off`).

Foreground gateway runtime forms such as `openclaw gateway`, `openclaw gateway run`, `openclaw gateway restart`, and `openclaw gateway --force restart` are treated as lifecycle mutations. Read-only inspection remains outside the guard, including `openclaw gateway status`, `openclaw gateway --help`, `openclaw gateway run --help`, `launchctl print`, `systemctl status`, `schtasks /Query`, and generic read-only process lookups. `openclaw gateway call` is method-aware: lifecycle RPCs such as `update.run` and `gateway.restart.request` require explicit lifecycle approval, while read-only RPCs such as `health`, `update.status`, and `logs.tail` do not.

The classifier also handles lifecycle commands hidden behind common command carriers, including nested `env`, `env -S`, shell wrappers, package runners, `find`/`xargs`, process-kill pipelines, known environment expansions, unknown partial environments that could expand to OpenClaw, and Node launcher forms without treating benign `node -e` / `node --print` script arguments as executable paths. The classifier remains out of `openclaw/plugin-sdk/infra-runtime`; the deprecated SDK shim now explicitly preserves the previous exec approval exports without exposing this internal lifecycle taxonomy as plugin API.

## User Impact

Operators get an extra human confirmation before an agent or auto-review path can stop, start, restart, run, delete, or uninstall the OpenClaw gateway/daemon in non-yolo configurations. Existing yolo-mode behavior, read-only status/query commands, and public plugin SDK export counts are unchanged.

## Evidence

Final branch head: `60c5d3e36085b90715022d8bd823a2fdc0e72aa8`  
Rebased onto upstream `main`: `bdfe2a4e60d344d89f946efbb26d6f6046a48258`

### Final-head live Gateway proof

A production build from the final head was started as an isolated loopback Gateway with temporary config/state and `auth=none`. The proof driver imported the production `processGatewayAllowlist` implementation from the same head. Port, temporary path, request id, and device identity were redacted.

```json
{
  "branchHead": "60c5d3e36085b90715022d8bd823a2fdc0e72aa8",
  "surface": "production processGatewayAllowlist with isolated config/state",
  "gatewayHealth": "healthy",
  "results": [
    {
      "name": "non-yolo lifecycle mutation",
      "command": "openclaw gateway restart",
      "security": "full",
      "ask": "on-miss",
      "autoReviewCalls": 0,
      "outcome": "forced onto explicit-approval registration before auto-review; the fresh isolated Gateway then rejected the unpaired scope upgrade",
      "hasLifecycleWarning": true,
      "warning": "OpenClaw lifecycle commands require explicit approval unless exec is running in yolo mode."
    },
    {
      "name": "yolo lifecycle control",
      "command": "openclaw gateway restart",
      "security": "full",
      "ask": "off",
      "autoReviewCalls": 0,
      "pendingStatus": null,
      "deniedStatus": null,
      "hasLifecycleWarning": false
    },
    {
      "name": "read-only control",
      "command": "openclaw gateway status",
      "security": "full",
      "ask": "on-miss",
      "autoReviewCalls": 0,
      "pendingStatus": null,
      "deniedStatus": null,
      "hasLifecycleWarning": false
    }
  ]
}
```

This demonstrates the requested final-head boundary: the non-yolo lifecycle mutation cannot reach auto-review, while the yolo mutation and read-only command retain their control behavior. The isolated device was intentionally not paired, so this proof does not claim that a human approved the request after registration. Maintainer confirmation of the intended non-yolo policy remains a separate product/security decision.

### Focused tests

```shell
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/infra/exec-approvals-lifecycle-positive-a.test.ts \
  src/infra/exec-approvals-lifecycle-positive-b.test.ts \
  src/infra/exec-approvals-lifecycle-env.test.ts \
  src/infra/exec-approvals-lifecycle-shell.test.ts \
  src/infra/exec-approvals-lifecycle-negative.test.ts
# Test Files  5 passed (5)
# Tests       525 passed (525)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts \
  src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts \
  src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts \
  src/utils/utils-misc.test.ts \
  --testNamePattern="OpenClaw lifecycle|gateway lifecycle RPC|durable allowlist|empty env operands|removes POSIX backslash line continuations"
# Test Files  4 passed (4)
# Tests       9 passed | 229 skipped (238)
```

### Static and CI validation

- Changed-file `oxfmt --check`: passed.
- Changed-file type-aware `oxlint`: passed.
- `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet --base bdfe2a4e60d344d89f946efbb26d6f6046a48258`: passed.
- `git diff --check bdfe2a4e60d344d89f946efbb26d6f6046a48258...HEAD`: passed.
- Linux Node 24 `check-test-types`: passed.
- CI max-lines ratchet, lint, production types, security checks, QA smoke profiles, and real behavior proof: passed.

The remaining red CI shard is an unrelated timeout in untouched `src/cli/acp-cli-exit.process.test.ts`; all other compact shards passed.
